Top SQL with Top Events

  • Top SQL statements by DB Time along with the top events by DB Time for those SQLs.
  • % Activity is the percentage of DB Time due to the SQL.
  • % Event is the percentage of DB Time due to the event that the SQL is waiting on.
  • % Row Source is the percentage of DB Time due to the row source for the SQL waiting on the event.
  • Executions is the number of executions of the SQL that were sampled in ASH.

Finding 1: Top SQL Statements
Impact is 1.43 active sessions, 17.57% of total activity.
---------------------------------------------------------
SQL statements consuming significant database time were found. These
statements offer a good opportunity for performance improvement.

   Estimated benefit is .88 active sessions, 10.81% of total activity.
   -------------------------------------------------------------------
   Action
      Investigate the PL/SQL statement with SQL_ID "9khk1b9ht609p" for
      possible performance improvements. You can supplement the information
      given here with an ASH report for this SQL_ID.
      Related Object
         SQL statement with SQL_ID 9khk1b9ht609p.
         begin PKG_CBVER02_RTGSAPI.PROC_GET_RTGSWEBREQSTAT(:1,:2,:3,:4,:5);

      0% for parsing, 0% for PL/SQL execution and 100% for Java execution.

         SQL statement with SQL_ID gvhbumfb6gsw3.
         INSERT INTO GLBKBPJ.TMPFRMTRN6 (GMST_CODE,OTHGMST,NRECNO,FORM60_61)

         WHERE :"SYS_B_00"=:"SYS_B_01"   AND A.GMST_CODE=B.GMST_CODE AND ( ( (
         DECODE(NVL(C.LINKGMST,:"SYS_B_02"),:"SYS_B_03",
         LTRIM(RTRIM(LPAD(NVL(UPPER(LTRIM(RTRIM(C.PANNO))),TO_CHAR(NVL(C.LINKG
         MST,C.GMST_CODE))),:"SYS_B_04",:"SYS_B_05"))),
         LTRIM(RTRIM(LPAD(NVL(TO_CHAR(NVL(C.LINKGMST,C.GMST_CODE)),UPPER(LTRIM
         (RTRIM(C.PANNO)))),:"SYS_B_06",:"SYS_B_07"))) ) =
         LTRIM(RTRIM(A.SRCHGRPID)) )
         OR ( UPPER(LTRIM(RTRIM(C.PANNO))) IS NOT NULL AND
         UPPER(LTRIM(RTRIM(C.PANNO)))= LTRIM(RTRIM(A.SRCHPANID))   )
         )      )
         UNION
         SELECT DISTINCT A.GMST_CODE AS GMST_CODE,C.GMST_CODE AS
         OTHGMST,B.NRECNO,C.FRM60_61 FROM
         (
         SELECT  DISTINCT A.GMST_CODE,NVL(B.LINKGMST,B.GMST_CODE) AS
         SRCHLINKGMST
         FROM BANKMAS B,GLBKBPJ.TMPFRMTRN7 A WHERE NVL(B.PANNO(+),:"SYS_B_08")
         = NVL(A.SRCHPANID,:"SYS_B_09")  AND
         UPPER(LTRIM(RTRIM(B.PANNO(+)))) IS NOT NULL
         AND NVL(B.LINKGMST(+),:"SYS_B_10") !=:"SYS_B_11" AND
         NVL(B.LINKGMST(+),B.GMST_CODE(+)) != A.GMST_CODE ) A,BANKMAS C
         ,GLBKBPJ.TMPFRMTRN5 B
         WHERE :"SYS_B_12"=:"SYS_B_13"  AND A.GMST_CODE=B.GMST_CODE AND
         ( NVL(C.LINKGMST,:"SYS_B_14")= NVL(A.SRCHLINKGMST,:"SYS_B_15") AND
         NVL(C.LINKGMST,:"SYS_B_16")<>:"SYS_B_17"   )

Finding 2: Session Connect and Disconnect
Impact is 1.24 active sessions, 15.29% of total activity.
---------------------------------------------------------
Session connect and disconnect calls were consuming significant database time.

   Recommendation 1: Application Analysis
   Estimated benefit is 1.24 active sessions, 15.29% of total activity.
   --------------------------------------------------------------------
   Action
      Investigate application logic for possible reduction of connect and
      disconnect calls. For example, you might use a connection pool scheme in
      the middle tier.


Finding 3: Soft Parse
Impact is 1.02 active sessions, 12.51% of total activity.
---------------------------------------------------------
Soft parsing of SQL statements was consuming significant database time.

   Recommendation 1: Application Analysis
   Estimated benefit is 1.02 active sessions, 12.51% of total activity.
   --------------------------------------------------------------------
   Action
      Investigate application logic to keep open the frequently used cursors.
      Note that cursors are closed by both cursor close calls and session
      disconnects.

   Recommendation 2: Database Configuration
   Estimated benefit is 1.02 active sessions, 12.51% of total activity.
   --------------------------------------------------------------------
   Action
      Consider increasing the session cursor cache size by increasing the
      value of parameter "session_cached_cursors".
   Rationale
      The value of parameter "session_cached_cursors" was "1000" during the
      analysis period.

Impact is .84 active sessions, 10.31% of total activity.

JAVA execution consumed significant database time.

      Look at the "Top SQL Statements" finding for SQL statements consuming
      significant time in Java execution. For example, the PL/SQL statement
      with SQL_ID "9khk1b9ht609p" is responsible for 100% of Java execution
      time during the analysis period.

Finding 6: Hard Parse Due to Invalidations
Impact is .53 active sessions, 6.52% of total activity.
-------------------------------------------------------
Cursors were getting invalidated due to DDL operations. This resulted in
additional hard parses which were consuming significant database time.

   Recommendation 1: Application Analysis
   Estimated benefit is .53 active sessions, 6.52% of total activity.
   ------------------------------------------------------------------
   Action
      Investigate appropriateness of DDL operations.

   Symptoms That Led to the Finding:
   ---------------------------------
      Hard parsing of SQL statements was consuming significant database time.
      Impact is .82 active sessions, 10.13% of total activity.


Finding 7: Undersized SGA
Impact is .5 active sessions, 6.18% of total activity.
------------------------------------------------------
The SGA was inadequately sized, causing additional I/O or hard parses.
The value of parameter "sga_target" was "143360 M" during the analysis period.

   Recommendation 1: Database Configuration
   Estimated benefit is .14 active sessions, 1.77% of total activity.
   ------------------------------------------------------------------
   Action
      Increase the size of the SGA by setting the parameter "sga_target" to
      152320 M.

   Symptoms That Led to the Finding:
   ---------------------------------
      Hard parsing of SQL statements was consuming significant database time.
      Impact is .82 active sessions, 10.13% of total activity.
      Wait class "User I/O" was consuming significant database time.
      Impact is .68 active sessions, 8.39% of total activity.
